We need to answer: "What United Kingdom Prime Minister was succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party?" The question is ambiguous. Likely asking: Which UK Prime Minister was succeeded (i.e., replaced) in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party. In the 1990s, the Conservative Party leader was John Major (became leader in 1990 after Margaret Thatcher). He succeeded Margaret Thatcher as Prime Minister in 1990. So the Prime Minister succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party (John Major) was Margaret Thatcher. Let's verify evidence.

We have evidence about 1997 Conservative Party leadership election triggered when John Major resigned after defeat at 1997 election. Also evidence about Margaret Thatcher being new Conservative Prime Minister in 1980 local elections. Not directly about succession. Need evidence that Margaret Thatcher was succeeded by John Major in 1990. Not present in given evidence. We have evidence: "These were the first annual local elections for the new Conservative Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher." That indicates she was PM before 1980. Not about succession.

We have evidence: "The Federation of Conservative Students ... in reference to then Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher". Not about succession.

We have evidence about John Major: "The 1997 Conservative Party leadership election was triggered ... when John Major resigned on 2 May 1997, following his party's defeat at the 1997 general election, which ended 18 years of Conservative Government of the United Kingdom." That indicates John Major was PM before 1997, succeeded by Labour. Not about who he succeeded.

We need evidence that John Major succeeded Margaret Thatcher as PM in 1990. Not present. Could there be evidence about Margaret Thatcher being PM before John Major? Not directly. The only mention of Margaret Thatcher is in local elections 1980 and Federation of Conservative Students referencing her. No explicit statement of succession.

Thus we cannot answer with evidence. The question: "What United Kingdom Prime Minister was succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party?" Could also refer to a Prime Minister succeeded by the Leader of the Conservative Party (i.e., the Leader of the Conservative Party succeeded the PM). In 1990s, the PM was John Major (Conservative) succeeded by Tony Blair (Labour) in 1997. But the Leader of the Conservative Party after Major was William Hague (1997). But the question phrasing: "What United Kingdom Prime Minister was succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party?" Could be asking: Which PM was succeeded by a Conservative Party leader (i.e., the successor was a Conservative Party leader). In 1990s, the PM John Major (Conservative) succeeded Margaret Thatcher (also Conservative). Both are Conservative Party leaders. But the phrase "by the Leader of the Conservative Party" suggests the successor was the Leader of the Conservative Party. In 1990, John Major became Leader of Conservative Party and PM, succeeding Margaret Thatcher. So answer: Margaret Thatcher.

But we lack citation. Could we use evidence that John Major was Conservative leader and Prime Minister? We have evidence: "Major had been Conservative leader and Prime Minister since November 1990." That's from the 1997 leadership election article: sentence 1: "Major had been Conservative leader and Prime Minister since November 1990." That indicates he became leader and PM in November 1990. It implies he succeeded someone. Not explicit but we can infer that he succeeded Margaret Thatcher. However we need citation that Margaret Thatcher was PM before him. We have evidence: "These were the first annual local elections for the new Conservative Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher." That shows she was PM before 1980. Not enough to show she was PM until 1990. But we can combine: Margaret Thatcher was PM (evidence). John Major became PM in November 1990 (evidence). So the PM succeeded in the 1990s by the Leader of the Conservative Party (John Major) was Margaret Thatcher. This is supported by two citations: one showing Thatcher as PM, another showing Major became PM in 1990. That indicates succession.

Thus answer: Margaret Thatcher.
